title: What If a Marathon Took 54 Years? One Olympic Runner's Really Did

scenes.text: What if you took 54 years to finish a marathon? One Olympic runner did.
Stockholm, 1912. Shizo Kanakuri of Japan had spent 18 days getting there by ship and train.
The race was run in a heat wave. Half the field never finished. Partway through, Kanakuri stopped at a house for a drink.
Then he quietly went home to Japan without telling the officials. In Sweden, he became the runner who vanished.
In 1967, Swedish television invited him back. He was in his seventies. He crossed the line.
Official time: 54 years, 8 months, 6 days, 5 hours, 32 minutes and 20 seconds. He said he'd had six children along the way.

description:
What if a marathon took 54 years to finish? Shizo Kanakuri of Japan started the Olympic marathon in Stockholm in 1912 and completed it in 1967.
He had travelled 18 days by ship and the Trans-Siberian Railway. The race was run in a heat wave and only 34 of 68 starters finished; Kanakuri stopped at a house along the route, was given a drink, and went home without notifying race officials, so Swedish records had him as missing. Invited back in 1967, he finished in 54 years, 8 months, 6 days, 5 hours, 32 minutes and 20.3 seconds, and said: it was a long trip; along the way I got married, had six children and ten grandchildren. He also ran at the 1920 and 1924 Games and is called the father of the marathon in Japan.
